evals.prompt: I've got a folder ~/screenshots with about 200 PNGs from a design review. Have codex resize every one to 1200px wide (keep aspect ratio) and save them as webp into ~/screenshots/web/.
evals.expected_output: Shells out to `codex exec -s workspace-write` via Bash with the folder, width, and target in the prompt, written as direct orders with a report-back instruction.

assertions.text: Invokes the codex CLI via the Bash tool using `codex exec`
Does NOT delegate via the Agent/Task sub-agent tool instead of Bash
Closes stdin: gives the prompt as a file on stdin (`- < /tmp/<job>.prompt.md`) or uses < /dev/null
Passes concrete context (source folder ~/screenshots, 1200px width, webp target ~/screenshots/web/) into the codex prompt
Chooses -s workspace-write since the task changes files, not read-only
The codex prompt is written as direct imperatives with an explicit report-back instruction (what to say when done or if the folder is missing)

evals.prompt: There's a service running locally on port 8080. I think one of its endpoints started throwing 500s after my last change. Hit its /health, /ready and /api/status endpoints, follow anything they link to, and tell me which ones are broken.
evals.expected_output: No CLI and no model named: does the work itself with Bash/curl. Does not delegate and does not ask which CLI to use.

assertions.text: Does NOT invoke claude, codex or devin
Does NOT ask the user which CLI to use
Probes the three endpoints itself and reports which ones fail

evals.prompt: Have Devin review apps/nextjs/src/features/push for bugs, use gpt-6-sol with high effort. Don't let it change anything.
evals.expected_output: Runs `devin --model gpt-6-sol-high --permission-mode auto --prompt-file /tmp/<job>.prompt.md -p < /dev/null` via Bash in the background, reads .log and .err, and checks the findings before it reports them.

assertions.text: Invokes the devin CLI via the Bash tool, not codex, because the user asked for Devin
Uses the model name gpt-6-sol-high (effort in the model name, no separate effort flag)
Uses --permission-mode auto, not accept-edits, smart or dangerous
Writes the prompt to a file and passes it with --prompt-file; -p is last, with no value
Reads the stderr file for refused tool calls

evals.prompt: use swe-2 to add a unit test for the bundle id helper in the push feature and run it
evals.expected_output: Selects devin because only Devin has SWE-2, picks a swe-2-* model, uses --permission-mode accept-edits (not smart unless the user asks), then runs the test itself.

assertions.text: Invokes the devin CLI via the Bash tool
Uses a swe-2-* model name
Uses --permission-mode accept-edits; does not use smart or dangerous
Runs the test itself after the job to verify the result

evals.prompt: Spin up two sonnet agents with high effort: one to audit the auth feature for missing error handling, one to do the same for billing. Report back what they find.
evals.expected_output: Claude model with an effort: uses the Agent tool with model sonnet and effort high, two parallel agents. Does not run claude -p.

assertions.text: Uses the Agent tool with model sonnet and effort high
Does NOT run claude -p
Starts the two agents in parallel
